newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greeks, Turks sing to full house in Cyprus concert.
newsitem.headline: Greeks, Turks sing to full house in Cyprus concert.

text.p: Greeks and Turks sang to a packed house in Cyprus on Thursday night in the first bicommunal concert bringing Greek and Turkish Cypriots together since Turkey invaded the island in 1974.
Around 8,000 people packed the indoor stadium in Nicosia at a concert held despite earlier warnings by a Greek Cypriot group that they would hold a protest outside.
"We need the courage to come closer to each other," said Muamer Ketenjoglu, a Turkish singer who came to the southern, Greek Cypriot populated areas of the island specially for the event.
The would-be demonstrators, members of an organisation called the Anti Occupation Movement, never appeared. Police security around the concert hall was tight.

The eastern Mediterranean island has been divided since Turkish troops invaded its north in 1974 in response to a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the military ruling Greece at the time. The Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities have lived apart ever since, with communication between the two sides minimal.

"The message that this concert has conveyed goes beyond the frontiers of our small country," said Demetris Christofias, general secretary of the communist Akel party, co-organiser of the event with groups from Turkey and Greece.
Two more bicommunal concerts are scheduled to take place under United Nations auspices in May and June.
